outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Few‑Shot Tabular Learning and LLMs
outline.description: Sets the stage by reviewing the challenges of learning from small tabular datasets, the rise of large language models (LLMs), and why combining them is promising.
subtopics: Why tabular data is hard in few‑shot regimes
Overview of large language models and in‑context learning
Prior work using LLMs for tabular prediction
Limitations of existing LLM‑based approaches

outline.chapter_title: Motivation for Feature Engineering with LLMs
outline.description: Explains the key insight of using LLMs as feature engineers rather than end‑to‑end predictors, and introduces the FeatLLM concept.
subtopics: From end‑to‑end LLM inference to rule generation
Benefits of extracting rules as features (latency, API‑only access, prompt size)
High‑level overview of the FeatLLM pipeline
Relation to ensemble and bagging ideas

outline.description: Formal definition of the few‑shot tabular classification setting used throughout the book and the notation that will be reused.
subtopics: Dataset definition (features, feature names, labels)
Few‑shot sampling (k‑shot) and evaluation metrics
Goal: learn a predictor from k examples using an LLM as a black‑box
Assumptions on feature descriptions and LLM access

outline.description: Detailed walkthrough of the three‑part prompt construction (basic info, reasoning instructions, response format) that guides the LLM to produce high‑quality rules.
subtopics: Basic information block: task description, feature names/types, few‑shot examples
Serialization of tabular rows into natural language
Reasoning instruction: two‑step chain‑of‑thought (causal inference then rule deduction)
Response instruction: exact format for rule output, handling logical operators
Prompt length considerations and feature‑bagging tricks

outline.chapter_title: Parsing Natural‑Language Rules into Binary Features
outline.description: Covers the challenges of converting noisy LLM output into executable code and the solution of using the LLM itself for code generation.
subtopics: Typical noise in LLM‑generated rules (symbol vs. word forms)
Designing a secondary prompt to ask the LLM to emit Python functions
Safe execution with exec() and handling errors
Creating the binary feature matrix Z_k for each class
Complexity analysis of the parsing step

outline.description: Shows how a simple linear model with non‑negative weights turns the binary rule features into class probabilities.
subtopics: Formulation of the linear scorer (logit = max(w,0)·z)
Softmax conversion to probabilities
Training objective: cross‑entropy on k‑shot data
Why positivity constraints improve interpretability
Optimization details (Adam, epochs, early stopping)

outline.description: Explains the ensemble strategy that mitigates rule noise, reduces prompt size, and improves robustness.
subtopics: Why a single LLM query may produce incomplete or noisy rules
Bagging of features and/or instances for each ensemble member
Temperature‑controlled diversity of generated rule sets
Aggregating predictions across T trials (average of probabilities)
Effect on computational cost and prompt length

outline.description: Practical guidance for reproducing FeatLLM, including API usage, hyper‑parameter choices, and debugging tips.
subtopics: Choosing an LLM backend (GPT‑3.5, alternatives)
Setting temperature, top‑p, and max tokens
Number of ensembles and rules per class – default values and trade‑offs
Training the linear layer (learning rate, batch size, k‑fold CV)
Debugging rule parsing failures

outline.description: Summarizes the empirical study across 13 diverse tabular datasets and compares FeatLLM with baselines.
subtopics: Dataset collection and characteristics (size, feature count, domain)
Baseline categories: classical ML, semi‑supervised, LLM‑based
Evaluation protocol (AUC, repeated splits, few‑shot settings)
Main results: performance gains and statistical significance
Analysis of where FeatLLM shines (high‑dimensional tables, low shot)

outline.description: Investigates the contribution of each design choice through systematic ablations.
subtopics: Removing weight tuning vs. simple rule count
No ensemble / no bagging
Omitting feature descriptions
Skipping the first reasoning step
Interpretation of results across shot numbers

outline.description: Explores how FeatLLM handles spurious correlations, noisy features, and hyper‑parameter sensitivity.
subtopics: Synthetic addition of irrelevant columns and performance impact
Rule quality metrics (AUROC of individual rules before/after tuning)
Effect of ensemble size and number of rules per class
Training and inference time comparison with other methods
Discussion of failure modes and mitigation strategies

outline.description: Shows how the rule‑based features provide transparent insight into model decisions.
subtopics: Reading the generated natural‑language rules
Inspecting learned weights to rank rule importance
Case studies: medical and financial datasets
Link to broader interpretability literature

outline.description: Discusses potential research directions and how to adapt the framework to new settings.
subtopics: Scaling to larger sample regimes (beyond low‑shot)
Generating richer feature types (embeddings, interaction terms)
Incorporating domain‑specific LLMs or fine‑tuned models
Combining FeatLLM with other tabular pre‑training methods
Handling bias and fairness in LLM‑derived rules

outline.description: Recaps the contributions of FeatLLM, its practical relevance, and societal considerations.
subtopics: Summary of methodological advances
Implications for real‑world low‑label domains (healthcare, finance)
Potential risks from LLM bias and misinformation
Guidelines for responsible deployment
